page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.xlarge is an x86_64 architecture instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 4 physical cores and 4 vCPUs with a single thread per core configuration. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and operates on a KVM hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that this instance sits in the lower performance tiers. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng and Geekbench rank in the bottom 10% to 25% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth tests show a significant drop-off from 163.7 GB/sec for small cached blocks to 19.6 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, reflecting potential memory subsystem bottlenecks. Similarly, database operations, static web serving, and text processing benchmarks consistently register in the bottom 10% tier.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.se1ne.xlarge is its high memory allocation paired with relatively weak processing capabilities. While it offers a generous 32.0 GB of RAM, the underlying Intel Xeon processor limits its suitability for compute-intensive tasks. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance is best positioned for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high CPU throughput, such as caching layers, lightweight database operations, or memory-heavy background processing where execution speed is secondary to memory capacity.
